glosses: A number of domestic animals assembled together under the watch or ownership of a keeper.

examples.text: a herd of cattle
a herd of sheep
a herd of goats
The lowing herd wind slowly o’er the lea.

glosses: Any collection of animals gathered or travelling in a company.

examples.text: Zakouma is the last place on Earth where you can see more than a thousand elephants on the move in a single, compact herd.
Zebras can also be called a herd or a zeal.

glosses: A crowd, a mass of people or things; a rabble.

examples.text: I was never one to follow the herd.
But far more numerous was the Herd of ſuch, / Who think too little, and who talk too much.
You can never interest the common herd in the abstract question.

There were herds of leather sofas and enough computers to ensure that no prospective matriculant or visiting parent could enter a room and not see at least one available keyboard, not even in the dining hall or field house.

glosses: To unite or associate in a herd; to feed or run together, or in company.

examples.text: Sheep herd on many hills.
The women bunched up in little droves and let their tongues clack, and the men herded together and passed a jug around and, to tell the truth, let their tongues clack too.
Any predator that preys on animals that herd or school, has to be able to single out one individual to attack.

glosses: To unite or associate in a herd
To manage, care for or guard a herd

examples.text: He is employed to herd the goats.

glosses: To associate; to ally oneself with, or place oneself among, a group or company.

examples.text:
I’ll herd among his Friends, and ſeem
One of the Number, […]
"[W]hy, I say, oh stranger, dost thou think that I herd here with barbarians lower than the beasts?"

glosses: To move, or be moved, in a group. (of both animals and people)

examples.text: On alighting at the station, we were all herded over the footbridge and through a side exit.

glosses: Someone who keeps a group of domestic animals.

examples.text: John Dodds, the herd who bode in the place, was standing at the door, and he looked to see who was on the road so late.
Any talent which gives a good new thing to others is a miracle, but commentators have thought it extra miraculous that England's first known poet was an illiterate herd.

glosses: To act as a herdsman or a shepherd.
To form or put into a herd.
To move or drive a herd.

examples.text: I heard the herd of cattle being herded home from a long way away.

translations.source_sense_description: Gruppe von meist größeren Säugetieren der gleichen Art

glosses: A number of birds together in a group, such as those gathered together for the purpose of migration.
A large number of animals associated together in a group; commonly used of sheep, but (dated) also used for goats, farmed animals, and a wide variety of animals.

examples.text: He told his father, and said it would be just suitable work for him to run about fields and woods amongst the strawberry hills after a flock of hares, and now and then lie down and take a nap on some sunny hill.

glosses: Those served by a particular pastor or shepherd.

examples.text: But lapsed into so long a pause again / As half amazed, half frighted all his flock: [...]
I also have other sheep that are not from this pen. I must lead them. They, too, will respond to my voice. So they will be one flock with one shepherd.

glosses: A large number of people.

examples.text: The heathen […] came to Nicanor by flocks.

glosses: A religious congregation.
To congregate in or head towards a place in large numbers.

examples.text: People flocked to the cinema to see the new film.

What place the gods for our repose assigned.
Friends daily flock; and scarce the kindly spring
Began to clothe the ground
Given the poor state of the line's trains and schedules, it is remarkable that people flock to use or experience it in embarrassingly large numbers.

glosses: To flock to; to crowd.

examples.text: Good fellows, trooping, flocked me so.

glosses: Coarse tufts of wool or cotton used in bedding.
A lock of wool or hair.

examples.text: I prythee, Tom, beat Cut's saddle, put a few flocks in the point.

glosses: Very fine sifted woollen refuse, especially that from shearing the nap of cloths, formerly used as a coating for wallpaper to give it a velvety or clothlike appearance; also, the dust of vegetable fibre used for a similar purpose.

examples.text: There was a neat hat-and-umbrella stand, and the stranger's weary feet fell soft on a good, serviceable dark-red drugget, which matched in colour the flock-paper on the walls.

glosses: To coat a surface with dense fibers or particles; especially, to create a dense arrangement of fibers with a desired nap.

examples.text: the sampling and elution advantages of flocked swabs versus spun swabs

glosses: To cover a Christmas tree with artificial snow.
To treat a pool with chemicals to remove suspended particles.

glosses: Troupe d’animaux sauvages

examples.text: Stubbs vit de grands troupeaux de singes.

glosses: Troupe d’animaux domestiques de même espèce, qui sont élevés et nourris dans un même lieu.

examples.text: Mais généralement l’envoi de quelques troupes met fin aux troubles en peu de temps. Elles envahissent le territoire de la tribu à châtier, pillent les douars, razzient les troupeaux, détruisent les cultures, font des prisonniers et coupent des têtes, […].
Avec leurs pommes de terre, leurs châtaignes et leur seigle, les paysans du Ségala engraissent de nombreux troupeaux de porcs dont ils tirent beaucoup d’argent.
Les nomades gardaient des troupeaux de yaks et de moutons appartenant en grande partie aux classes privilégiées.

glosses: Troupeau de moutons ou de brebis.

examples.text: L’écho de la forêt voisine répétait nos cris, le mugissement des troupeaux, le tintement des clochettes et le claquement du fouet […].

glosses: Réunion de fidèles sous la direction d’un pasteur spirituel.

examples.text: Le troupeau de l’évêque, du curé. Le bon pasteur donne sa vie pour son troupeau.

glosses: Troupe, d’une multitude de personnes.

examples.text: Nous sommes l’ancre du salut, le havre de la bourgeoisie ; car nous conduisons le troupeau des humains avec la peur de l’inconnu, nous savons les paroles mystiques qui brisent les énergies, domptent les volontés et forcent la bête humaine à lâcher la proie pour l’ombre.
Il fut démontré qu’il avait touché pour ne rien dire des agissements d'une banque, laquelle, […], saignait cruellement le troupeau des épargnants cupides et malfaisants.
En aval de la mosquée, un troupeau de prostituées, commandées de service par le pacha, nous salua de grêles you-yous destinés à nous donner l’illusion d’une manifestation spontanée des femmes de Fez.
Le nouveau était particulièrement poignant quand il poussait l’incongruité jusqu’à arriver en cours d’année scolaire au lieu de se joindre au troupeau de septembre.

glosses: Ensemble d'éléments semblables, assimilables à un troupeau d'animaux.

examples.text: J’ai regardé un moment par le hublot le défilement paresseux d’un vaste troupeau de nuages […].
